events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The driver cancelled and the platform charged the rider a $6.61 no-show fee, so NS-0 routes the case to NS-1/NS-2 [F3][F6][NS-0]. The rider disputes being a no-show, and both advocates now accept the same facts.

NS-1 requires all three elements. Element (i) is met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:05:55 [F5]. Element (ii) fails: at the moment of the tap the GPS put him 601 m from the pickup, and his closest approach over the whole trip was 545 m, never inside 200 m [F5][F1][NS-1]. Element (iii) also fails: after the tap he spent 0 s continuously inside the pickup radius — his 3 min 30 s stationary period was served 600 m away [F5][F2][NS-1]. The platform timeline corroborates this: driver_arrived_at is null, so the driver was never recorded at the pickup point [F4][NS-1].

The driver's chat assertion that he was "here already" and his written statement that he waited at the pickup are claims contradicted by the system records (GPS, timeline), and system records prevail over statements; the rider's contemporaneous 12:06 message saying she was at the pickup point and saw no car is consistent with those records [F8][F12][F9][F1][F2][F4][NS-2].

Because NS-1 (i)–(iii) are not all satisfied, the $6.61 fee does not stand and is refunded in full [F3][F6][NS-2]. The amount is the cancellation fee on record: $6.61 [F6][NS-2], with no surge component (surge multiplier 1.0×) [F7]. No traffic incident, speed-band record or weather event exists to explain the driver's position [F13][F14][F15].

The trace's NS-2 limb is also triggered: the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius [F5][F1][NS-2], which warrants account review alongside the refund. The profile facts (clean driver record, clean rider record) are not used to decide the case and cannot defeat the measured tap position [F16][F17][NS-2][NS-7].

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the tap), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 545 m and the GPS track never puts him within 200 m of it, so condition NS-1(ii) fails.
The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:05:55 while 601 m away from the pickup point and then stayed within 200 m for 0 s, so the arrival he claimed was false.
The driver's 3 min 30 s of stationary time was spent 600 m from the pickup point, not at the pickup, so NS-1(iii) (waiting more than 3 minutes at the pickup point) also fails.

The driver's written statement that he 'waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup' is contradicted by the GPS record and the platform timeline, and the rider's own message at 12:06 says she was at the pickup point and saw no car; the system records win over the statement.
Because NS-1 (i)-(iii) are not all satisfied, the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee charged on record must be refunded in full under NS-2.

The driver pressed the arrival button while GPS showed him 601 m from the pickup point and then cancelled as a no-show, an abuse of the arrival/cancellation button under Ryde's fraud list, which warrants an account flag alongside the refund.

weaknesses: NS-1(i) is satisfied: the driver did press "I'm Here" at 12:05:55 (F5), and the conflict message F8 at 12:06 claims he was already there, so the driver will argue he complied with the button requirement and that the app arrival indicator rather than GPS should be trusted.

The driver waited 3 min 30 s stationary before cancelling (F2) and the whole episode took 7 min 5 s (F3), so the driver will argue he gave the rider ample time and that the rider simply did not come out, pointing to F9 as admission the rider was waiting but never boarded.

The driver's record is clean — 4.84 rating, 502 trips, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F17) — which the other side will use to argue the mis-tap was a one-off GPS/app error rather than button abuse, weakening my flag_account request.
I cannot prove where the rider physically stood: there is no rider-side location fact, so the rider's claim of waiting at the pickup point rests only on her own chat message F9.

claims.assertion: The driver did tap "I'm Here", but the system record shows the tap occurred at 12:05:55 while he was 601 m from the pickup point, and he spent 0 seconds inside the 200 m pickup radius after it — so NS-1(ii) is not satisfied.
GPS never places the driver at or near the pickup point: his closest approach was 545 m at 12:05:20 and he never came within 200 m of the pickup point for the whole trip.
The 3 min 30 s the driver waited was spent stationary at (1.3040, 103.8584), 600 m from the pickup point, not at the pickup point as NS-1(iii) requires.
The platform never recorded the driver's arrival at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), corroborating the GPS record that he was never there.
Because NS-1 (i)–(iii) are not all satisfied, the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee does not stand and must be refunded in full to the rider.

The rider's contemporaneous message at 12:06 ("I'm at the pickup point and I don't see any car") is consistent with the GPS record that no car was within 200 m, while the driver's own chat at 12:06 asserted he was already there — the driver's written statement (F12) loses to the GPS record.
There is no external cause for the driver's position: no traffic incidents, no speed-band records and fair weather were recorded on the route during the trip window.
The driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints in 90 days (502 trips), and the rider has 0 disputes in 90 days, so no flag_account request is made against either party on this record.

weaknesses: The driver did press the "I'm Here" button (F5), which he will cite as showing he intended to wait; F5 also shows the tap was made 601 m away with 0 s inside 200 m, which is what defeats NS-1.

The driver's chat #1 at 12:06 (F8) and his written statement (F12) both assert he was at the pickup point; the rider may use these to argue the driver was genuinely present, but F1/F2/F4 (system records) contradict them and system records win.

The driver waited a real 3 min 30 s (F2), so he can argue the waiting duration element of NS-1(iii) was met on its own — but that element is not met "at the pick-up point", so the fee still cannot be sustained under NS-1.[F2][F5]

points.response: Conceded: the driver's own side now agrees the "I'm Here" tap at 12:05:55 was made 601 m from the pickup point with 0 s inside 200 m (F5), so NS-1(ii) fails exactly as I argued in C2.
Conceded: the driver accepts GPS never brought him within 200 m of the pickup point, closest 545 m at 12:05:20 (F1), which is the factual basis of my C1.
Conceded: the driver accepts his 3 min 30 s wait was served 600 m from the pickup point (F2), so NS-1(iii)'s "at the pick-up point" element is unmet, as in my C3.
Conceded: the null driver_arrived_at (F4) is undisputed and reinforces C1 that the driver was never recorded at the pickup point.
Conceded in substance and adopted: the opposing brief itself concludes the $6.61 fee cannot stand and asks for refund_full of $6.61 (F3, F6) under NS-2, which is precisely my requested outcome.

Conceded: the rider's 12:06 message saying she was at the pickup point and saw no car (F9) is, on the opponent's own reading, consistent with GPS and outweighs the driver's claim of presence in F8/F12, supporting C4.
Conceded: the absence of any incident, speed-band or weather record (F13, F14, F15) removes any external excuse and is not contested by me; it does not change the NS-2 outcome.

Disputed in part: I do not rely on the profile history to prove the fee is invalid — the fee fails on F1, F2 and F5 alone — but the driver's clean record (F17) is no answer to his arrival button being pressed 601 m from the pickup point (F5), which is why my C6 flag_account request stands as an add-on, not the finding.
Conceded — F1 shows the closest approach was 545 m and the driver never entered 200 m, so NS-1(ii) fails; my client does not contest the refund, only the finding of deliberate button abuse.

The tap did happen at 12:05:55 with 0 s inside 200 m (F5), but that shows an early/location-mismatched tap, not a fabricated arrival; NS-1 fails on the location element and NS-2 refunds the fee, while the separate account-flag limb of NS-2 requires the tap plus GPS showing him outside the pickup point — a threshold my client's 873-day, 502-trip, zero-dispute record (F17) does not meet as abuse.

Accepted as to the location of the waiting time (F2, 600 m from pickup) but not as to motive: my client did wait 3 min 30 s and cancelled after 7 min 5 s (F3), which is the conduct of a driver who believed he was at the right place, not one engineering a no-show fee.
Conceded on the conflict — F12 is a claim and yields to the GPS and timeline records (F1, F2, F4), so the driver's version of being at the pickup point cannot be sustained.

Agreed on the outcome: because NS-1 (i)–(iii) are not all met, the $6.61 on record (F3, F6) falls under NS-2, and the rider gets refund_full of $6.61 — which is also the outcome I request for my client.

Contested as far as it seeks an account flag: my client's 90-day record shows 502 trips with 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F17), and a single early arrival tap outside the radius (F5) is at most a mis-press, not the 'remaining stationary and uncontactable' abuse NS-2 points to; the fee is refunded, no flag is warranted.
